meaning:
ἐξ-ορύσσω
[in LXX: Pro.29:22; ὀφθαλμόν (-ούς), Jdg.16:21, 1Ki.11:2 (נָקַר)* ;]
to dig out, dig up: στέγην, Mrk.2:4; metaphorically, ὀφοαλμούς (cf. LXX, ll with; Herod., viii, 116), Gal.4:15.†
(AS)

renderings.kjv: when they had broken it up

elsewhere.note: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic…
What was the blessing you enjoyed? For I testify to you that, if possible, you would have plucked out your eyes and given them to me.
